title: Deployment mode evaluation — Retail search POC
content:
Purpose:
This note captures the outcomes from the deployment-mode evaluation session (10/28/2025) for the Retail Search POC. It is intended to help the customer and internal stakeholders decide which Redwood deployment mode (hosted API, dedicated, or private) to use for the 6-week proof of concept and what the staged architecture should look like.

Context and customer constraints: 
- Customer: Mid-market retail SaaS (search + personalization). Sensitive PII in product data but not regulated PHI/PCI.
- POC goals: demonstrate 95th percentile tail latency < 200ms for query rewriting + reranking at synthetic load ~150 QPS, and show cost/per-query under $0.006 for production-like traffic.
- Security: must support VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. Data residency: EU only for customer’s EU tenants.
- Timeline: 6-week POC, demo at week 5.

Evaluation summary (short):
- Hosted API: Fastest on-boarding, lowest engineering lift. Good for early functional validation and cross-region demos. Risks: shared tenancy may conflict with customer-managed KMS and strict data residency expectations; no SLA for dedicated throughput.
- Dedicated: Best balance for POC->pilot transition. Predictable throughput, can allocate GPU types to meet latency targets, supports VPC peering and customer-specific capacity. Higher cost than hosted but allows realistic performance testing at scale.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Highest control and compliance. Longer lead time and heavier ops. Consider only if customer requires full isolation or has strict procurement prohibitions with cloud providers.

Decision criteria we applied:
- Performance fidelity: How closely the environment mimics production throughput, caching behavior, and networking.
- Time-to-demo: How quickly we can get a stable, demoable system.
- Security/compliance fit: KMS, VPC, data residency, audit log access.
- Observability: access to tracing, token-level cost, and model-level dashboards for debugging.
- Cost predictability: ability to reserve capacity or predict per-token spend for SOW pricing.

Recommendation (POC path): staged approach to reduce risk and meet timeline
1) Week 0–2: Hosted API (fast functional validation)
   - Purpose: validate prompt templates, rewrites, and reranking logic end-to-end with sample dataset.
   - Deliverables: end-to-end flow working, latency baselines, initial cost estimates, demo script.
   - Constraints: use anonymized EU-hosted endpoints where possible; avoid sending raw customer PII during early tests.
2) Week 2–4: Dedicated capacity (realistic performance test)
   - Purpose: validate throughput at 150 QPS, stress KV cache behavior, test autoscaling/burst policy.
   - Config: 2x A100-equivalent GPUs (or recommended instances), quantization profile from Optimize review, prefix caching enabled.
   - Deliverables: perf report (p95, p99), cost per-query with committed capacity, rollback policy for model fallbacks.
3) Week 4–6: Harden + pilot handoff (optional private trial for EU-only tenancy)
   - Purpose: if customer requires, spin private deployment in EU region or VPC peering. Otherwise finalize Dedicated -> pilot SOW.

Architecture sketches (high level):
- Hosted stage: Redwood API endpoint (eu-west region) -> CDN edge -> customer UI/service. Use tokenization and sample KV caching on client side for prefix caching tests.
- Dedicated stage: VPC peered Redwood Dedicated cluster in EU region. Deploy separate model variant for reranker with quantized weights; enable tracing to console dashboards; configure autoscale min=1, max=4 for steady-state tests.
- Private stage: customer-managed VPC with Private control plane; include KMS integration and audit syslog forwarder.

Risk mitigations and test plan:
- Data leakage: anonymize real PII during hosted tests; enable strict allowlist on endpoints.
- Performance variance: run 3x load tests at different times of day; capture KV hit rates and model latency distribution.
- Model regressions: baseline eval set for reranker; block rollout of new model if quality drop > 3% NDCG@10.

Operational checklist for POC:
- Observability: enable per-request tracing, token-level cost breakdown, real-time dashboard for p95/p99.
- Security: verify VPC peering and KMS access for Dedicated stage; collect SOC2 audit request list if private is requested.
- Cost controls: set quota for hosted test traffic; reserve Dedicated capacity to avoid noisy neighbor impact.
- Rollouts: create canary route for reranker; prepare automatic fallback to smaller model when latency > 300ms.

Open questions for the customer (to resolve in kickoff):
- Do you require customer-managed KMS for the POC or only for pilot/prod?
- Is EU data residency required for the POC demo or only for pilot/prod?
- Expected real-world QPS distribution (peak vs baseline) beyond synthetic 150 QPS target?
- Procurement / contract constraints that would block Dedicated capacity reservation?

Next steps and owners:
- Aisha: prepare Hosted API demo workspace and anonymized dataset (due: Week 0+3 days).
- Miguel: capacity sizing proposal for Dedicated (due: Week 1).
- Claire: security questionnaire draft and KMS checklist to send to customer (due: Week 1).
- Benji: load test harness and perf runbook (due: Week 2).

Notes and context links: refer to linked artifacts above. For detailed autoscale tuning see runtime playbook PR in the linked GitHub. Meeting notes captured in Slack thread (linked).

Appendix (quick cost and latency heuristics we used):
- Heuristic per-query costs assume dedicated GPU amortized across reserved vGPU slots; numbers vary with quantization and batching.
- Latency target mapping: A100-class w/continuous batching + KV cache typically meets p95<120ms for 512-token workflows; reranker-only flows can be <80ms when CPU-based reranker is used.

If customer confirms KMS + EU residency requirement, default to Dedicated for POC to ensure fidelity and avoid late rework into Private. Otherwise start with Hosted for speed.

-- end of brief --
